answer: The fable cap is upheld at intake and quill makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch however much capital it holds, because each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a kernel tag. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
